label: input c late in the original phase of sequences that start with r (or g)
explanation: A very sparse feature (221 activations in 1M sequences, almost all weak). 96% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=4-7 and none is in the copy phase. About 80% of mass is on input c, and the first original token is r (79% of mass) or g (18%). It fires harder when the prefix also contains b, z, n or w, e.g. r g b z n c, which is the max at 3.37. The previous token is often n or z. The rest is weak firing on other tokens (0, 2, f, p, <DEL>) in similar r/g...b/z/n prefixes. It does not fire at t<4, in the copy phase, or on c in most sequences. The core predicate has about 0.76 mass recall but precision near 0.03, because most late c inputs in r/g-initial sequences stay silent. Adding prefix-set conditions raises precision only to about 0.2, at the cost of recall. The feature seems to pick out a narrow conjunction of prefix contents that per-step variables do not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 35 cues. Raise it: orig0=r (+4.29), orig0=g (+2.68), phase=0 & in_tok=c (+2.18), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=c (+2.18), orig1=g (+2.12), orig2=b (+1.90). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.27), phase=2 (-1.69), t=3 (-1.51), prev3_tok=r (-1.05).
